subject.title: [Bug]: OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM disable semantics unclear; LaunchAgent still appends after unset/0

question: Should explicit launchd or managed-service disable values for `OPENCLAW_RAW_STREAM` override persisted state-dir `.env` and config-generated service env values, or should persisted durable env remain authoritative until edited?
rationale: Raw-stream logs can contain private prompts, tool output, and user data, so automation should not choose the precedence rule for a sensitive diagnostic logging boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Explicit Disable Wins
options.body: Treat `unset`, `0`, `off`, `false`, and explicit service disable intent as authoritative, clear or override stale generated raw-stream service-env entries, and document that precedence.

options.title: Durable Env Wins
options.body: Keep state-dir `.env` and config service env as the authoritative managed-service source, and document that operators must remove those values before restart disables raw-stream logging.

options.title: Doctor/Status Repair Only
options.body: Leave runtime precedence unchanged but add doctor/status warnings and repair guidance when stale raw-stream service env can make logging appear disabled while still active.

recommendation.title: Explicit Disable Wins
recommendation.body: Treat `unset`, `0`, `off`, `false`, and explicit service disable intent as authoritative, clear or override stale generated raw-stream service-env entries, and document that precedence.

likelyOwner.reason: The raw-stream runtime and central service-env helper history both route most strongly through steipete's recent work.
